name: Asymmetric Dimensional Disguise
description: I broke the perfect symmetry of the three sets in the 3-Dimensional Matching problem. By presenting two of the sets as rows and columns of a grid, and the third set as distinct items to be placed on that grid, the problem strongly pattern-matches to 2D Bipartite Matching (Rook Placement). Models that rely on surface features will likely write a polynomial-time Max Flow or Hopcroft-Karp algorithm instead of the required exponential DFS, causing them to fail on test cases where the flow network's arbitrary perfect matching does not align with the module constraints.
